subject: Tier selection & feature-bridging for Clearspring pilot
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Amira Patel <amira@clearspring.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tier selection & feature-bridging for Clearspring pilot

Amira —

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. Per our discussion, I wanted to outline three quick paths for the Clearspring pilot and get confirmation on which constraints matter most for you: predictable throughput (SLA), cost ceiling during pilot, or feature parity for recognised production capabilities (vector search + private models).

Options (high level):
- Elastic pilot (lowest up-front cost): metered tokens + burst pool. No guaranteed SLA; rollback to baseline model if saturation.
- Anchored tier (predictable throughput): reserved capacity for pilot hours, 99th pct latency SLA, includes prefix cache and 1:1 support.
- Hybrid bridge (recommended): reserved baseline + elastic burst with a stepped step-down credit if Clearspring drops usage below threshold within first 60 days. Ensures feature parity while reducing cost risk.

Questions for you:
1) Is guaranteed throughput (latency SLO) non-negotiable for demo traffic?
2) Do you need an explicit downgrade credit if you step down within the first 30–60 days? If so, what $ amount would move the needle?
3) Any procurement constraints on contract length (monthly vs 12-month)?

I've attached a short worksheet (Clearspring-pilot-questions.xlsx) — please fill the expected daily peak qps and 99th pct latency target so we can surface a concrete price/credit.

I'll loop Ben into the next note with a proposed credit structure and a sample canary rollout.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0192

From: Amira Patel <amira@clearspring.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Clearspring Procurement <procurement@clearspring.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Tier selection & feature-bridging for Clearspring pilot

Jonas —

Thanks — the worksheet is helpful. Quick answers inline:
1) Predictable throughput is important for the initial clinical demo next month; we can tolerate up to 150ms 95th but would prefer <300ms 99th.
2) Yes, a downgrade credit is meaningful to procurement. We don't have a firm $ target yet — the team would respond to something in the 10–20% of committed monthly fee range for early rollback protection.
3) Procurement prefers 12 months but will accept an initial 3 month pilot with an option to convert. We need clear exit/fallback terms.

Also: Can you confirm whether the hybrid bridge supports private model variants (we need the data isolation for test transcripts)? If not, the anchored tier is the likely path.

Amira
Amira Patel
Head of Product, Clearspring Health
amira@clearspring.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Amira Patel <amira@clearspring.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Sep 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tier selection & feature-bridging for Clearspring pilot

Amira — thanks for the quick responses. Based on the latency targets and procurement preference, here's a concrete recommendation and our proposed guardrails:

Recommendation: Hybrid bridge (reserved baseline + burst) with private-model flag enabled on the reserved nodes. This gives you isolation and lets you scale during peak demos.

Pricing & credits (example):
- Baseline reserved: $9,000/month (baseline capacity for pilot hours — covers expected demo QPS up to 75 qps).
- Elastic burst pool: metered at $0.009/token beyond baseline.
- Early-downgrade credit: if Clearspring cancels or reduces the reserved baseline within 60 days, Redwood provides a step-down credit equal to 25% of the remaining 2 months on the reserved fee (capped at $4,000).
- SLA holdback: 5% of monthly invoice held as credit if 99th pct latency > target for more than 3 business days.

Canary plan:
- Week 0 (onboarding): private-model deployment to staging; run synthetic load to verify latency and KV cache warm-up.
- Week 1 (canary): route 10% of demo traffic to the pilot for two business days. If 99th < 300ms, expand to 50% for three days.
- Week 2: full routing for demo windows; monitor for two weeks.

Attachments: tier-matrix-v2.pdf (contains the capacity breakpoints and a visual of the stepdown credit math).

If that sounds reasonable, Jonas — can you prepare a short MSA amendment that includes the early downgrade credit language? I can put the pricing numbers into a quote in HubSpot and send a DocuSign for the pilot P0.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Tier selection & feature-bridging for Clearspring pilot

Amira —

This plan sounds like a good, pragmatic compromise. Next steps (mutual action plan):
1) Clearspring: complete attached worksheet with peak QPS and confirm demo dates by Mon 09/06.
2) Redwood: Ben will push a HubSpot quote (CLSPR-2026-09) with the hybrid pricing and the early-downgrade credit. Target to have DocuSign ready by 09/08.
3) Technical canary: schedule a 60 minute runbook session (tentative 09/10) to run the synthetic validation and KV cache warm-up.
4) Legal: I'll draft an MSA amendment adding the 60-day step-down credit and the SLA holdback language; Marissa to review for approval.

If all good, I will include the DocuSign link in the next email.

Thanks — looking forward to getting Clearspring live for the demo.

—Jonas
